newsitem.title: BOSNIA: NATO did not see indicted Karadzic vote in Bosnia.
newsitem.headline: NATO did not see indicted Karadzic vote in Bosnia.

text.p: The U.N. confirmed on Sunday that indicted war criminal Radovan Karadzic voted in Bosnia's post-war elections but NATO's peacekeeping commander said his men did not spot him.
Karadzic, who led the Bosnian Serbs during the 43-month war, voted near Pale in eastern Bosnia on Saturday, the U.N. spokesman said, quoting "local sources".

But the commander of NATO peace forces in Bosnia, mandated to arrest those indicted by the U.N. war crimes tribunal in The Hague if they are spotted during patrols, said his men did not see Karadzic vote.

The former Bosnian Serb president was eligible to cast a ballot as a registered citizen of Bosnia without a criminal conviction and did so in mid-afternoon in Brakovac, part of the Pale municipality, the spokesman said.

Admiral Joseph Lopez, commander of NATO's 53,000-strong peace force which guarded routes to polling stations throughout Bosnia on election day, told a news conference: "We have no reports of (NATO) seeing Karadzic."
Alex Ivanko of the International Police Task Force, or U.N. monitors, said: "The voter on the most wanted list voted at polling station No. 6 in Brakovac between 3 and 4 p.m."
"It was apparently a small polling station in a relatively rural area and no international (observers) were around to my knowledge," he told Reuters.
U.N. sources who asked not be named said the information came from "reliable Serb political channels".
Karadzic, who has laid low since quitting Serb politics in July under international pressure, has not been touched although NATO troops regularly patrol his base town, Pale.

Critics have accused NATO of turning a blind eye to movements by Karadzic and other prominent indicted Serb war criminals, who usually have well-armed bodyguards, to avoid confrontations that might cause NATO casualties.
True reconciliation between Bosnia's Moslem, Serb and Croat communities will never happen as long as indicted war criminals roam free, most analysts say.
Karadzic has been indicted for genocide and crimes against humanity in connection with the separatist Serb siege of Sarajevo and massacre of Moslems from Srebrenica.
